memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'And now let Pharaoh look for a discerning and wise man and put him in charge of the land of Egypt. Let Pharaoh appoint commissioners over the land to take a fifth of the harvest of Egypt during the seven years of abundance. They should collect all the food of these good years that are coming and store up the grain under the authority of Pharaoh, to be kept in the cities for food. This food should be held in reserve for the country, to be used during the seven years of famine that will come upon Egypt, so that the country may not be ruined by the famine.'" - Gen 41:33-36 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph does not stop at interpreting the dream; he offers wise, practical counsel. Since seven years of plenty are coming, followed by seven of famine, the answer is clear: store up grain during the good years so there will be food during the hard ones. Set aside a portion in the abundance, and the nation will survive the famine. It is simple, godly wisdom — and it would save countless lives.

Here we see that faith and practical wisdom belong together. Joseph trusted God's word about the future, and then he acted wisely in light of it. He did not say, "God will provide, so we need do nothing." He said, in effect, "God has shown us what is coming; now let us prepare responsibly." Trusting God and planning wisely are not opposites.

There is a timeless principle here: prepare in the good times for the hard times. Scripture praises the ant who "stores its provisions in summer and gathers its food at harvest" (Prov 6:8). When life is abundant, it is wise to save, to build reserves, to strengthen ourselves for leaner seasons that may come. Wisdom does not spend everything the moment it arrives.

This applies to more than money. In seasons of spiritual abundance, we store up truth and strengthen our faith, so that in seasons of famine and trial, we have reserves to draw on. Use your "seven good years" well. Prepare, while you can, for the harder days.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I preparing in good times for possible hard times?
2. Do I hold faith and practical wisdom together?
3. What "reserves" — financial or spiritual — should I be building now?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, give me wisdom to prepare in seasons of plenty for seasons of need. Help me to trust You and to plan wisely, storing up what will sustain me and others in harder days. Amen.
